summary: Extends the Session Description Protocol so that applications using WebSocket as their transport can describe the connection they want. It adds an attribute that carries the WebSocket connection URI. This lets endpoints negotiate such sessions in the same way they negotiate other media or data connections.

eli5.summary: Before two friends talk on a special phone line, they swap a note with the phone number. This adds a place on the note for a WebSocket address.

questions: how to signal websocket connections in sdp
what is the sdp websocket-uri attribute
which side opens the websocket connection in sdp
subtitle: A new SDP attribute that tells a WebSocket client which URI to connect to.

tldr.problem: When an application uses WebSocket as a transport and SDP to negotiate, there is no standard place in the SDP to say which URI the WebSocket client should connect to.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8124 defines the media-level attribute a=websocket-uri, whose value is a ws or wss URI, and sets rules for the offer/answer exchange and the client.
tldr.outcome: Applications such as BFCP over WebSocket can advertise the connection URI in a common way. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 8124 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2017, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why SDP Needs a WebSocket URI
sections.content:
The WebSocket protocol (RFC 6455) lets clients and servers exchange messages over a persistent TCP connection, optionally secured with TLS. Several specifications use a WebSocket subprotocol as a reliable transport, for example for SIP (RFC 7118), MSRP (RFC 7977), XMPP (RFC 7395) and BFCP.

When such a subprotocol is used between a server and a client, the connection URI must be passed from the server to the client. For applications that already negotiate with the Session Description Protocol (SDP, RFC 4566), RFC 8124 does this with an SDP attribute.
sections.eli5: If you are going to a friend's house you need the address. This document says where in the call setup note the address goes.

sections.title: The websocket-uri Attribute
sections.content:
The new SDP media-level attribute websocket-uri can appear in any media section. Its value is the ws-URI or wss-URI defined in Section 3 of RFC 6455. The RFC's example is a=websocket-uri:wss://example.com/chat.

When the attribute is present, the IP address in the c= line SHALL be ignored and the full URI SHALL be used to open the connection. Clients MUST ignore both the c= address and the port in the m= line.

For multiplexing, the attribute is in the CAUTION category. The RFC says bundling WebSocket is technically possible but impractical and unlikely to be used, so no multiplexing rules are specified.
sections.eli5: The note now has a line holding the exact web address to connect to, and the old phone-number-style lines are ignored.

sections.title: Offer and Answer Procedures
sections.content:
An endpoint that wants WebSocket MUST say so in the proto field of the m= line, for example TCP/WSS/BFCP over TLS or TCP/WS/BFCP without. The server side, whether offerer or answerer, MUST add an a=websocket-uri attribute. Either side can start the connection, and the setup attribute is set following RFC 4145.

The offerer SHOULD use active or passive for setup and MUST NOT use holdconn; with passive it MUST include the URI. The answerer likewise MUST NOT use holdconn. If it answers active, it starts the WebSocket handshake toward the URI. If it answers passive, it MUST supply a ws or wss URI.

To change a session, either side MAY send a new offer. The existing connection can be reused with a=connection:existing if the URI and transport parameters are unchanged; otherwise a new connection is negotiated. For an offerless INVITE, the server MUST offer with setup set to passive and include the URI.
sections.eli5: The two sides agree who will dial and who will wait, and the one who waits must give out the address.

sections.title: What the WebSocket Client Does
sections.content:
The WebSocket client MUST always initiate the outgoing TCP connection, so its setup attribute is always active. The WebSocket server is a server on the Internet, so it MUST always use passive. The RFC notes this also avoids the need for ICE, since the model is a typical client-to-server web connection.

After the offer/answer completes, the client MUST start the WebSocket handshake by sending a GET toward the URI, following RFC 6455. If the URI has no port, the default port (80 or 443) is used depending on whether it was a ws or wss URI.
sections.eli5: The visitor always knocks on the door, and the house always waits. If no door number is written, the default door is used.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
An attacker may add, modify or remove an a=websocket-uri attribute, which could make an application misbehave. The RFC therefore RECOMMENDS integrity protection for session descriptions; for SIP, S/MIME is available.

Application signalling over WebSocket MUST support secure WebSocket and SHOULD use it. The client MUST follow RFC 7525, including host name verification, when setting up TLS with the server.
sections.eli5: Someone could swap the address on the note to trick you, so the note should be sealed and you should check you reached the right house.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: IANA registered websocket-uri in the SDP Parameters registry as a media-level attribute with long-form name WebSocket Connection URI. Its multiplexing category is CAUTION, it is not charset dependent, and its value is a ws-URI or wss-URI as defined in Section 3 of RFC 6455.
sections.eli5: The new line was written into the official list of allowed note lines.

messages.label: SDP offer
messages.note: WS or WSS in the proto field, setup:active.

messages.label: SDP answer
messages.note: setup:passive and a=websocket-uri with the connection URI.

messages.label: GET (WebSocket handshake)
messages.note: Sent toward the URI from the answer.
